angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,154,862 km at 177.65 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6292 +/- 0.0116 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 177.65 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.66 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Brahm et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-481 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..235B/abstract): 1,154,862 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.14 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Brahm et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-481 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..235B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5735 +/- 72 K from Brahm et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-481 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..235B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Brahm et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-481 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..235B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-481.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.055, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
